extracted.intended_audience: museum professionals and organizations applying to the IMLS Museums for America FY2023 grant program
extracted.subtask_short: IMLS Museums for America grant application
extracted.subtask_description: Preparation and submission of a Museums for America (IMLS) grant application (NOFO FY2023), including required attachments, conditionally required documents, compliance certifications, and materials that reviewers will evaluate.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of Key Project Staff
rubrics_metrics.description: List only those staff and consultants whose expertise is essential to the success of the project and save it as a PDF. This list must include the Project Director listed in Item 7 of the SF-424S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not list all staff involved in the project. If you cannot identify key project staff by the application deadline, list the position title(s) instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resumes of Key Project Staff and Consultants
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a resume of no more than two pages for each individual whose expertise is essential to the success of the project; include the Project Director's resume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Save all resumes in a single PDF. If key staff cannot be identified by the deadline, provide position description(s) including qualities, range of experience, and education necessary to implement and complete project activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of Nonprofit Status (conditionally required)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applying as a private, nonprofit institution (Applicant Type code 'M' in SF-424S), provide a copy of the IRS letter indicating eligibility for nonprofit status under the Internal Revenue Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must submit this letter with each application even if you have submitted it previously. State sales tax exemption letters are not acceptable proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Federally Negotiated Indirect Cost Rate Agreement (conditionally required)
rubrics_metrics.description: If using a federally negotiated indirect cost rate in your budget, provide a copy of your current Final Federally Negotiated Indirect Cost Rate Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit this letter with each application whether previously submitted or not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Products Plan (conditionally required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-page maximum plan describing types of digital products, and addressing availability, access, and sustainability for each type when proposing to generate digital content, resources, assets, or software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Guidance for Creating a Digital Products Plan. If selected for funding, the plan may be published online or otherwise shared by IMLS; do not include sensitive, proprietary, or confidential information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservation Treatment and Planning Documentation (conditionally required)
rubrics_metrics.description: When proposing conservation treatment, provide a document identifying conservation priorities and describing how they were established, plus detailed condition reports and/or treatment proposals for each object/specimen/group to be treated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable documents include a Conservation Assessment for Preservation (CAP) report, a Preservation Assistance Grant (PAG) report, a General Conservation Survey Report (prior IMLS-funded), similar survey reports funded locally/regionally/privately, or a current Long-range Conservation Plan approved by administration/governing body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting Documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may submit a reasonable number of supporting documents that supplement the Narrative in support of the project description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supporting documents should help reviewers envision the project in greater detail but should not introduce new topics or continue answers to Narrative questions. Give each document a clear, descriptive title. Examples: letters of commitment; bibliography/references; letters of support; relevant images; exhibit design plans; planning reports; contractor quotes; equipment specifications; past project products/evaluations; departmental plans; web links; needs assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration Requirements (UEI, SAM, Grants.gov)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submitting, an applicant organization must have a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), a current and active SAM registration, and an active Grants.gov registration with an approved Authorized Organization Representative (AOR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check registrations well in advance; Grants.gov registration can take several weeks and generally cannot be completed in a single day. The Grants.gov user ID and password are required to submit an application. Allow time to register and do not wait until the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission Method and Deadline Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: All organizations must submit applications using Grants.gov Workspace; do not submit via email or postal mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants.gov will accept Museums for America applications through 11:59 p.m. U.S. Eastern Time on the stated deadline (example: November 15, 2022). IMLS may allow deadline extensions for organizations adversely affected in declared disaster areas. IMLS makes grants only to eligible applicants that submit applications, including attachments, through Grants.gov on or before the deadline as indicated by Grants.gov date stamp. Grants.gov generates confirmation emails and provides application tracking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may use IMLS funds and cost share only for allowable costs as found in IMLS and OMB government-wide cost-principle rules (see 2 C.F.R. part 200 and 2 C.F.R. part 3187).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of generally allowable costs: personnel salaries, wages, fringe benefits; travel for key project staff and consultants; materials, supplies, software, equipment directly related to project activities; adaptive/assistive technologies; equipment to improve collections storage and exhibit environments; third-party costs; publication design/printing; program evaluation; staff and volunteer training; paid internships/fellowships; indirect/overhead costs. Applicants must explain all proposed expenses in the Budget Justification. Consult 2 C.F.R. guidance for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unallowable Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain costs are not allowable for IMLS funds or cost share under this announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of unallowable costs: general fundraising costs (development office staff/time for fundraising); contributions to endowments; general operating support; acquisition of collections (see 2 C.F.R. § 3187.15(b)); general advertising or PR solely for promotion (other than project-related); construction or renovation involving construction trades (generally not allowable); social activities, ceremonies, receptions, entertainment; research projects (see 2 C.F.R. § 200.1). If unsure whether an activity is allowable, contact IMLS staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs for Third Parties (contractor vs subrecipient determination)
rubrics_metrics.description: When federal funds are paid to third parties (partners, consultants, vendors, service providers), the applicant must determine whether the third party is a subrecipient or a contractor and reflect that characterization in the terms of agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 2 C.F.R. § 200.1 for definitions and 2 C.F.R. § 200.331 for subrecipient/contractor determinations. IMLS grant funds may not be provided to any federal agency serving as a third party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect Costs Options
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may choose how to account for indirect costs in the budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options: use a negotiated federal indirect cost rate (not to exceed current rate); use an indirect cost rate proposed to a federal agency for negotiation (if finalized by award time); use the de minimis rate of 10% of Modified Total Direct Costs (if no negotiated rate and not otherwise required); or not include any indirect costs. Click IMLS links for further information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Justification (review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate whether the applicant selected an appropriate program goal/project category and associated objectives, whether project advances the museum’s strategic plan, and whether the need/problem is described using relevant data and best practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key reviewer questions: Has the applicant selected the appropriate program goal and objectives? Are the ways the project advances the museum's strategic plan specific and measurable? How well has relevant data and best practices been used to describe the need/problem/challenge? Has the applicant appropriately defined target group(s) and beneficiaries? Were target groups and stakeholders appropriately involved in planning? For Collections Stewardship and Access projects: Are the collections/records and their current condition described and quantified in enough detail?

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Work Plan (review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers assess whether proposed activities are informed by relevant theory and practice; goals, assumptions, and risks are clearly stated; staff and partners have the necessary experience; and resources and timelines are realistic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer questions include: Are proposed activities informed by relevant theory/practice? Are goals, assumptions, and risks clearly stated? Do identified staff/partners/consultants/service providers have the experience and skills necessary? Are time, financial, personnel, and other resources realistic for scope/scale? Is the proposed Performance Measurement Plan likely to generate required measures of Effectiveness, Efficiency, Quality, and Timeliness? If a Digital Products Plan is present, does it reflect appropriate practices and standards for creating/managing the proposed digital products? Will methods for tracking project progress allow course adjustments and produce reliable, measurable information about results?

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Results (review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate whether intended results are clearly articulated, realistic, meaningful, linked to the need, and whether plans to effect change and sustain benefits are sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key points: Are intended results realistic, meaningful, and linked to the addressed need? Is the plan to effect change in knowledge/skills/behaviors/attitudes solidly grounded and appropriately structured? Is it clear the federal investment will generate identifiable societal benefits? Will products be made available and accessible to the target group? Is the plan to sustain project benefits beyond the period of performance reasonable and practical? For Collections Stewardship and Access projects: Will care, condition, management, access to, or use of collections and/or records improve as a result?

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review Process and Selection
rubrics_metrics.description: IMLS uses a peer review process: professionals with relevant expertise evaluate complete applications according to the review criteria; peer reviewers must comply with IMLS federal ethics and conflicts of interest requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director considers peer review input and makes final funding decisions consistent with agency mission and programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated Integrity and Performance System Review (FAPIIS/SAM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to making federal awards above the simplified acquisition threshold, IMLS must review information in the designated integrity and performance system (accessible through SAM, e.g., FAPIIS) about the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may review and comment on information about themselves in the system. IMLS will consider applicant comments along with other information when assessing applicant integrity, business ethics, and record of performance per 2 C.F.R. § 200.206.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with Federal Administrative and Policy Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Award recipients are subject to 2 C.F.R. part 200 (Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements), 2 C.F.R. part 3187, the IMLS General Terms and Conditions for Discretionary Awards, and the IMLS Assurances and Certifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be familiar with these requirements and comply with applicable law. Failure to comply may result in suspension/termination of award and return of funds. See IMLS General Terms and Conditions and 2 C.F.R. § 200.340 for award termination information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must submit interim and final financial and performance reports according to the award reporting schedule using the IMLS electronic grants management system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports may be made accessible on the IMLS website. Recipients must also comply with debarment/suspension reporting (2 C.F.R. §§ 180.335 and 180.350) and other regulations. For awards with federal share > $500,000, refer to 2 C.F.R. part 200, Appendix XII and mandatory disclosure provisions (2 C.F.R. §§ 200.113, 200.211(c)(iii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledging IMLS Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees must include an acknowledgement of IMLS support in all grant products, publications, websites, and presentations developed with IMLS funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All work products should reference IMLS and include associated grant award number(s). Use the Grantee Communications Kit for guidance on fulfilling these requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of Information in Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: IMLS may share grant applications, products, and reports to further agency mission and development of museum/library services; information in funded applications may be made public except privacy-protected information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify any information you deem confidential/proprietary and seek to have it protected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: As non-federal entities, award recipients must follow IMLS conflict of interest policies for federal awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Click IMLS guidance for more information; applicants and recipients are responsible for compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination Certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorized representative certifies applicant will comply with nondiscrimination statutes and implementing regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: Title VI (race/color/national origin and LEP access), Section 504 (disability), Title IX (sex in education programs), Age Discrimination in Employment Act, and any other applicable nondiscrimination statutes. See IMLS guidance on LEP access and applicable regulations (e.g., 45 C.F.R. part 1181 for Section 504).

rubrics_metrics.name: Debarment and Suspension Certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant certifies that neither it nor its principals are excluded/disqualified, convicted of certain offenses in the past three years, indicted/charged for listed offenses, or have had public transactions terminated for cause within the preceding three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must comply with 2 C.F.R. part 3185 and 2 C.F.R. part 180. If unable to certify, attach explanation. Primary tier participants must communicate these requirements to next lower-tier participants and comply with verification/communication requirements for contracts funded by IMLS awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Debt Status Certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorized representative certifies that the applicant is not delinquent in repayment of any federal debt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification is to the best of the authorized representative's knowledge and belief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drug-Free Workplace Certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant certifies it will provide or continue to provide a drug-free workplace in compliance with 2 C.F.R. part 3186 (which adopts the Government-wide implementation in 2 C.F.R. part 182).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes making a good faith effort to maintain a drug-free workplace; publishing a drug-free workplace statement; establishing a drug-free awareness program; actions regarding employees convicted of drug offenses; and identifying known workplaces under federal awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trafficking in Persons Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant certifies compliance with trafficking in persons requirements set out in the General Terms and Conditions for IMLS Discretionary Awards (2 C.F.R. § 175.15).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a condition of award and must be adhered to if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification Regarding Lobbying Activities (>$100,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applicants requesting funds in excess of $100,000, the authorized representative certifies that no federal appropriated funds have been paid or will be paid to influence federal officials in connection with the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If funds other than federal appropriated funds are paid to influence, submit Standard Form LLL (Disclosure of Lobbying Activities). Include certification language in award documents for all subawards and require subrecipients to certify/disclose accordingly. Failure to file required certification can result in civil penalties ($10,000–$100,000 per failure).

rubrics_metrics.name: General Certification of Compliance with Federal Laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorized representative certifies applicant will comply with all applicable requirements of other federal laws, executive orders, regulations, and policies governing the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This certification is material to award determination and binds the applicant and its authorized representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subawards and Contracting Restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Under IMLS regulations (2 C.F.R. § 3187.14), a recipient may not make a subaward unless expressly authorized by IMLS; recipients may contract for supplies, equipment, and services subject to applicable law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients planning to use awards to fund contracts must comply with communication and verification provisions in Debarment and Suspension requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act (NAGPRA) Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorized representative certifies applicant will comply with NAGPRA (25 U.S.C. § 3001 et seq.) if the organization controls or possesses Native American human remains, associated funerary objects, and/or cultural items and receives federal funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies even when funding is for a purpose unrelated to NAGPRA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historic Properties / Section 106 Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorized representative certifies applicant will assist the awarding agency in ensuring compliance with Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act and related preservation laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also references Exec. Order No. 11593 and other applicable preservation obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental Protections Certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant certifies project will comply with environmental standards including NEPA measures and multiple executive orders and statutes related to environmental quality, wetlands, floodplains, coastal zone management, clean air conformity, safe drinking water, endangered species, and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific items listed include: (a) NEPA environmental quality control measures; (b) Exec. Order 11738 violating facilities notification; (c) protection of wetlands (Exec. Order 11990/12608); (d) floodplain evaluation (Exec. Order 11988/12148); (e) Coastal Zone Management Act consistency; (f) Clean Air Act conformity to State Implementation Plans; (g) Safe Drinking Water Act protections; (h) Endangered Species Act protections. Also includes Wild and Scenic Rivers Act compliance and Flood Disaster Protection Act flood insurance purchase requirements where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research on Human Subjects Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable, applicant certifies project will comply with 45 C.F.R. part 46 regarding protection of human subjects in research, development, and related activities supported by the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact IMLS for further information; follow Institutional Review Board and human subjects protections as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research on Animal Subjects Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable, applicant certifies project will comply with the Animal Welfare Act (7 U.S.C. § 2131 et seq.) pertaining to care, handling, and treatment of warm-blooded animals held for research, teaching, or other activities supported by the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow applicable animal welfare regulations and institutional policies.
